issues.subcategory: effect-size conversion and synthesis for repeated-measures design
issues.description: The manuscript meta-analytically combines two Hedges' g values and then converts the pooled value to Cohen's f for a repeated-measures ANOVA without providing the formula, assumptions, or whether the g values are standardized mean differences for dependent samples. Converting between g and f in within-subjects designs depends on the dependence structure and the exact parameterization; using a simple conversion can materially misstate the required sample size. This undermines the claimed adequacy of power for the replication aim.
issues.quote: The existing results as regards effect sizes are Hedges’ g = 1.92, N = 55 (Ito et al., 2019) and Hedges’ g = 0.38, N = 74 (Kękuś et al., 2020). Given the rather large difference in effect sizes between both studies, random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13. This amounts to a Cohen f of about 0.57.

issues.subcategory: power analysis ignores dyadic clustering
issues.description: The power analysis treats the sample as 240 independent participants, but participants are tested in pairs, discuss with each other, and are assigned to conditions by pair. Outcomes of two members of a pair are statistically dependent. Ignoring clustering inflates the effective sample size and yields anticonservative power estimates and standard errors. The unit of randomization appears to be the pair, so analyses should account for nesting or use pair-level/cross-classified models.
issues.quote: The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs)... Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups... a sample of 240 participants was assumed; this allows for excellent power to detect medium and large effect sizes but not small ones.

issues.subcategory: failure to model non-independence within pairs
issues.description: Because each participant's misinformation exposure is generated through interaction with a specific partner, observations are not independent. Yet the planned analysis is a standard two-factor ANOVA at the participant level, with no random effect for pair and no dyadic modeling. This violates model assumptions and can bias p values and confidence intervals.
issues.quote: The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA, with one within-subjects factor with two levels (discussed vs. non-discussed items) and one between-subjects factor with four levels (three groups of methods of reducing memory conformity and the control group).

issues.subcategory: pair-level randomization but individual-level analysis mismatch
issues.description: Conditions are assigned at the pair level, but the analysis and power planning are described at the participant level. This creates a unit-of-analysis error. The effective between-subjects sample size is the number of pairs, not individuals, unless dyadic dependence is explicitly modeled.
issues.quote: Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups... The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs).

issues.subcategory: intervention heterogeneity confounds interpretation
issues.description: The three interventions differ on multiple dimensions beyond the target mechanism: content, modality, length, cognitive load, emotional salience, and direct instructions about the target task. For example, the Demonstration and motivation condition includes an additional memory task plus personalized feedback, whereas other conditions are podcasts. Any condition differences cannot be attributed cleanly to the theorized mechanism rather than to engagement, fatigue, stress, or time-on-task differences.
issues.quote: First, in order to demonstrate to participants that they are vulnerable to influence, a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used... Next, the participants’ motivation to resist memory suggestibility will consist in them listening to a podcast... In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.subcategory: control condition not matched for task demands
issues.description: The control condition is a neutral podcast, but one intervention includes an active memory task (DRM), written recall, individualized feedback, and motivational instructions. This leaves major uncontrolled differences in arousal, effort, self-relevance, and metacognitive activation. A proper control would need to match format and task engagement.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes... First... a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used... The subjects will also receive a worksheet to write down all the words they remember from the lists.

issues.subcategory: mismatch between theorized mechanism and measured construct
issues.description: The intervention hypotheses hinge on participants' awareness of discrepancies/source monitoring, yet no direct measure of discrepancy detection, source memory, or confidence calibration is included as a primary moderator/mediator. Therefore the study cannot test the central proposed mechanism and risks overinterpreting any observed effects.
issues.quote: Thus, we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies... our methods of reducing memory conformity are directed towards the participants who are aware of the discrepancy between both the original information and the misinformation obtained from the partner.

issues.subcategory: missing operationalization of discrepancy awareness
issues.description: The manuscript repeatedly theorizes about participants 'aware of discrepancies' but does not specify how awareness will be assessed, coded, or analyzed. Without an operational definition, this key construct is not measurable or reproducible.
issues.quote: Thus, we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies.

issues.subcategory: ambiguous primary outcome among multiple indices
issues.description: The plan lists four indices from the open-ended test and also mentions average accuracy on filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions, but does not clearly specify which outcome is primary for hypothesis testing, how multiplicity will be controlled, or which index defines 'memory conformity'. This creates substantial researcher degrees of freedom.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers. Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test’s average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions.

issues.subcategory: undisclosed multiple comparisons strategy
issues.description: The manuscript proposes omnibus interactions and pairwise follow-up comparisons among four groups and multiple dependent variables but does not state any correction for familywise error or false discovery. This increases the risk of false positives.
issues.quote: In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed.

issues.subcategory: exclusion based on exposure creates post-randomization selection bias
issues.description: Excluding participants who 'did not hear any potentially misleading information' after randomization may induce selection bias, particularly if exposure rates differ across conditions or participant characteristics. Such exclusions can also distort the estimand from intention-to-treat to a selected complier subset. The manuscript does not plan to report how many are excluded per group or to conduct sensitivity analyses.
issues.quote: In addition, participants who are not exposed to co-witness details at all (that is, the participants who did not hear any potentially misleading information from the partner) will be excluded from the analyses.

issues.subcategory: replacement of excluded participants after viewing data
issues.description: Replacing excluded participants after data collection to 'maintain the correct sample size' is problematic because exclusion depends on post-experimental responses and may differ by condition. This can compromise randomization, introduce selection bias, and make the final sample contingent on observed data rather than prespecified recruitment with transparent flow reporting.
issues.quote: If any of the participants correctly guesses our hypotheses, they will be excluded from the analysis and replaced with another person in order to maintain the correct sample size.

issues.subcategory: selective exclusion based on hypothesis awareness likely differential by condition
issues.description: The authors acknowledge that awareness-based exclusion may be more common in experimental than control groups, but dismiss it as less important. This is a serious concern because differential exclusion after treatment can create artifactual group differences. The plan lacks a blinded coding procedure, threshold for 'correctly guesses our hypotheses,' and sensitivity analyses including all participants.
issues.quote: We realize that this may result in more exclusion in the three experimental groups than in the control group; however, this seems to be less important than potential problems arising from analyzing results from participants who realized that they are being misled.

issues.subcategory: no coding rules for open-ended responses
issues.description: The primary test uses open-ended responses, but no detailed coding manual is provided for classifying answers as correct, misinformation-consistent, other, or missing. Open-ended scoring can be subjective, especially for paraphrases or partial answers, making reliability and replicability impossible to evaluate without explicit criteria.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers (consistent with the movie), (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers (consistent neither with the movie nor the misinformation), and (4) the overall number of answers.

issues.subcategory: no interrater reliability plan for scoring and discussion coding
issues.description: Open-ended test responses and audio-recorded discussion classifications ('misleading', 'disputed', 'non-disputed') require human coding, yet no coder blinding, number of coders, training, or interrater reliability statistics are specified. This is essential for confidence in the primary outcome.
issues.quote: The discussion will be audio recorded... each answer given by the partner of a participant that is inconsistent with what the participant was presented with is misleading... their answers will be coded as “disputed”.

issues.subcategory: inconsistent count of critical items in collaborative recall
issues.description: The manuscript states that the film versions differ in eight critical details, but the collaborative recognition test includes only four critical-detail questions and eight control questions. Later, the main within-subject comparison is discussed as accuracy on discussed versus non-discussed critical items. The relation between the 12 collaborative questions, the 8 critical details, and later scoring is not sufficiently coherent and risks confusion about what is manipulated and analyzed.
issues.quote: Both versions are identical except for eight critical details... The test will comprise 12 questions, four of which refer to critical details... Immediately after... they will complete the individual memory test... eight of which will cover all the critical details included in the movie, regardless of whether they were subsequently discussed.

issues.subcategory: unclear intervention duration equivalence
issues.description: The two podcast interventions are described as approximately 7 minutes, but the Demonstration and motivation condition includes DRM administration, recall, feedback, and a podcast with no total duration reported. Unequal delay between misinformation exposure and final memory test could itself affect memory conformity, confounding condition differences.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast... The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast... First... a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used... Next, the participants’ motivation... will consist in them listening to a podcast

issues.subcategory: mechanistic claims unsupported by design
issues.description: The discussion of expected effects attributes any reduction to abandonment of the consistency assumption, increased alertness, improved source monitoring, or motivation. However, none of these mediators are measured, so causal claims about why an intervention worked would be unsupported. The design only permits testing whether conditions differ, not the proposed mechanism.
issues.quote: we assumed that the extended warning would cause participants to abandon the consistency assumption, make them more alert to discrepancies between their memories and information provided by the partner, and consequently cause them to rely on their own knowledge

issues.subcategory: DRM false recall as proxy for susceptibility to co-witness influence
issues.description: The exploratory use of DRM performance as a predictor of MORI memory conformity assumes shared vulnerability across paradigms, but DRM false recall taps associative gist-based false memory, whereas co-witness conformity involves social influence, source monitoring, and discussion dynamics. Without a stronger rationale, this predictor may have weak construct overlap and be difficult to interpret.
issues.quote: As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique.

issues.subcategory: no blinding of coders or experimenters reported
issues.description: Because the interventions are administered by the experimenter and outcomes include coded open-ended responses and discussion recordings, lack of blinding can introduce expectancy effects at administration and scoring stages. No blinding procedures are reported for participants beyond the movie deception, for experimenters, or for coders.
issues.quote: The discussion will be audio recorded... Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test... Next, the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was.

issues.subcategory: missing randomization procedure details
issues.description: The manuscript says pairs will be randomly divided into four groups but provides no information on sequence generation, allocation concealment, blocking/stratification, or how age matching within pairs is implemented before assignment. These omissions prevent assessment of selection bias and reproducibility.
issues.quote: Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups... After that, the third phase will take place... The participants will be randomly divided into four groups

issues.subcategory: possible contamination from pairwise joint intervention administration
issues.description: It is unclear whether members of each pair receive the intervention together or separately. If together, they may continue influencing each other during the intervention phase, especially in conditions involving explicit warnings about the partner, thereby altering the social dynamic in uncontrolled ways. This is particularly relevant because the unit is the pair and social influence is central to the phenomenon.
issues.quote: After that, the third phase will take place: it will consist in the procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation... Participants in the ‘Extended warning’ group will listen to the podcast... those in in the ‘Education about memory’ group will listen to the podcast...

issues.subcategory: missing details on administration context of interventions
issues.description: The manuscript does not state whether podcasts are delivered individually or jointly, via headphones or speakers, in the same room or separated, and whether participants can communicate during the intervention. These details are critical because social interaction itself may alter conformity and because differential administration may affect standardization.
issues.quote: participants will listen to the podcast... participants will listen to a podcast... In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.subcategory: confusion between recognition and recall terminology
issues.description: The second phase is described as a 'collaborative recognition test' with multiple-choice answers discussed aloud, while the study is elsewhere framed as collaborative recall. This matters because recognition and recall involve different memory processes, and the terminology inconsistency obscures the operational task used to induce misinformation.
issues.quote: After that, in the second phase, the participants will complete the collaborative recognition test... thanks to which the participants will discuss half of the discrepant details included in the original material, thus leading to mutual misinformation.

issues.subcategory: outcome metric may conflate memory conformity with response production
issues.description: One of the four planned indices is the 'overall number of answers' in an open-ended test. This reflects response withholding, verbosity, or guessing tendencies rather than memory conformity per se. Treating it alongside conformity-relevant outcomes risks construct contamination and post hoc interpretation.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers... (4) the overall number of answers.

issues.subcategory: ANOVA on bounded count data likely inappropriate
issues.description: The primary outcomes are small counts of correct/misinformation/other answers out of only eight critical items. Such data are bounded, discrete, and likely non-normal with heteroskedasticity, making standard ANOVA a poor fit. Generalized linear mixed models or binomial/multinomial models would be more appropriate, especially with repeated measures and pair clustering.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers... The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA

issues.subcategory: ignoring item-level variability
issues.description: The analyses aggregate across items and compare discussed versus non-discussed details, but critical items can vary substantially in baseline difficulty and susceptibility to conformity. Without modeling item as a random factor or at least reporting item-level analyses, effects may reflect idiosyncratic item composition rather than the intervention.
issues.quote: The correctness of answers to questions concerning discussed and non-discussed details will be compared... The efficacy of a given method will be confirmed if the magnitude of memory conformity (expressed as the difference between the accuracy on discussed and non-discussed items) is smaller

issues.subcategory: underpowered for small interaction effects despite theoretical ambition
issues.description: The authors acknowledge the study cannot detect small effects for the critical interaction. Given that intervention effects in social-cognitive memory research are often small-to-moderate and warnings have previously produced inconsistent results, the design may be underpowered for the main substantive question. This increases the chance of inconclusive null findings.
issues.quote: Considering the accessible financial, organizational and time resources, a sample of 240 participants was assumed; this allows for excellent power to detect medium and large effect sizes but not small ones.

issues.subcategory: real-world applicability claim not directly supported
issues.description: The rationale for placing interventions after misinformation exposure is 'to make our research closer to real life settings,' but the actual interventions (podcasts, DRM demonstration, explicit mention of court testimony) are artificial and may not resemble forensic practice. The design does not justify strong claims about practical witness-interview procedures without testing ecologically valid implementations.
issues.quote: The main reason for that is that we wanted to make our research closer to real life settings... But it is always possible to undertake some efforts in order to prevent a witness from reporting misinformation just before the interrogation.

issues.subcategory: restricted age range limits applicability to eyewitness populations
issues.description: Participants are limited to ages 16–35, excluding older adults who are highly relevant in eyewitness contexts and may differ in suggestibility and source monitoring. The paper does not sufficiently temper claims about eyewitnesses generally.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old... The age of the participants will be restricted

issues.subcategory: volunteer sample from media/internet advertisements
issues.description: Recruitment via media and internet advertisements likely yields a convenience sample that may differ from actual witnesses in motivation, stress, education, and familiarity with psychology experiments. The manuscript frames implications broadly for justice systems without acknowledging this limitation.
issues.quote: they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.

issues.subcategory: misapplication of normative influence dismissal
issues.description: The manuscript largely dismisses normative influence because the final test is individual, but normative pressures can persist after the discussion via commitment, desire for consistency, relationship maintenance, or internalized social influence. This oversimplifies the mechanisms of memory conformity and may bias interpretation of results.
issues.quote: Given the fact that the individual memory test does not include any element of direct interpersonal pressure, we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect has little use in this study

issues.subcategory: intervention overlap acknowledged but not theoretically resolved
issues.description: The authors acknowledge substantial conceptual overlap among interventions but do not define how they differ mechanistically or what pattern of results would distinguish theories. This weakens the confirmatory value of comparing them and leaves the study largely descriptive.
issues.quote: we are aware of some overlap between the three interventions, for instance, teaching about memory is included is present in a way in both Education about memory and Demonstration and motivation. Empirical results may help to determine to what extent the overlap is substantial

issues.subcategory: missing materials/scripts for interventions
issues.description: The content of the podcasts, exact wording, examples used, and DRM lists are not fully specified. Because subtle wording differences are central to warning efficacy, lack of full scripts prevents replication and evaluation of whether interventions differ only as intended.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast... The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast... Four lists will be chosen which on the basis of our previous research with this procedure, produce the strongest effect.

issues.subcategory: selection of strongest DRM lists based on prior unspecified research
issues.description: The plan says four DRM lists will be chosen because they 'produce the strongest effect' based on previous research, but does not specify the source, criteria, or whether this was preregistered before seeing current data. Selecting materials for strong effects without transparent rules can inflate apparent intervention potency and reduce reproducibility.
issues.quote: Four lists will be chosen which on the basis of our previous research with this procedure, produce the strongest effect.

issues.subcategory: unclear handling of confidence ratings
issues.description: Participants provide confidence ratings for each answer, but the analysis plan does not state whether or how these ratings will be analyzed. This is a missed opportunity given the theoretical emphasis on confidence and source trust, and it leaves an important collected variable underreported.
issues.quote: for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0%... to 100%

issues.subcategory: filler questions introduced only in analysis plan
issues.description: The analysis plan refers to 'filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions,' but the final memory test is described as containing 20 open-ended questions with eight critical details; the composition and purpose of filler questions in that final test are not described in Methods. This inconsistency obscures what outcomes will actually be analyzed.
issues.quote: Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test’s average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions.

issues.subcategory: no missing-data plan beyond exclusions
issues.description: There is no plan for handling item nonresponse, partial answers, missing confidence ratings, audio failures, or participants who provide 'don't know' responses on some items. Since open-ended tests commonly produce partial missingness, the absence of a missing-data strategy limits interpretability and reproducibility.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived... and (4) the overall number of answers... We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.subcategory: technical exclusions undefined
issues.description: The authors state they will exclude participants for 'any technical problems' but do not define thresholds, categories, or whether exclusions will be blind to condition/outcome. Vague technical exclusion criteria permit discretionary removal of cases and can bias results.
issues.quote: We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.subcategory: potential deception check confound at study end only
issues.description: Demand awareness is assessed only after the final memory test, and participants who infer hypotheses are excluded. This does not prevent expectancy effects during the task and instead creates post hoc sample selection. A better design would standardize demand characteristics and analyze awareness as a moderator rather than excluding participants.
issues.quote: Next, the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. If any of the participants correctly guesses our hypotheses, they will be excluded from the analysis

issues.subcategory: intervention bundles prevent attribution to active ingredients
issues.description: Each condition contains multiple components (e.g., extended warning includes warning, education, source-monitoring encouragement, confidence framing, and enlightenment; demonstration includes DRM feedback plus motivational message). Because components are bundled, any effect cannot be causally attributed to the named ingredient.
issues.quote: the following ideas were included... a clear warning... an extensive lecture... information about the possibility of confusing sources... information that many people do... give answers consistent with external sources... an enlightenment regarding the purpose of the deception.

issues.subcategory: overstatement that false memories will not be reduced
issues.description: The manuscript states it does not expect the proposed methods to reduce errors if false memories are involved, yet some interventions explicitly target source monitoring and metacognitive control, which could in principle affect false-memory reporting even if not underlying memory traces. The conceptual distinction between memory change and report bias is not clearly maintained.
issues.quote: As for false memories... In this case we do not expect that our proposed methods will make a memory report less contingent on false information provided by a co-witness.

issues.subcategory: broad justice-system implications from low-stakes lab task
issues.description: The manuscript repeatedly ties the findings to court judgments and witness interrogation, but the study uses a short silent film, low stakes, immediate testing, and convenience-sample dyads. These features differ substantially from real eyewitness situations involving stress, delay, repeated interviews, and heterogeneous witnesses.
issues.quote: Due to the serious consequences of inaccurate testimonies, research on methods of reducing the memory conformity effect is extremely important for the proper functioning of justice systems... But it is always possible to undertake some efforts in order to prevent a witness from reporting misinformation just before the interrogation.
